every_world.title: Loops of flow in every world
every_world.caption: Each dot is one world, over iterations 900–999 (400–499 for a world that did not live to 1,000), a column per kind of world; the bar is the median. Top left: how much of what agents stake on their neighbours a greedy search can put on closed loops, before a token one way and a token back cancel. Top right: what is left once they cancel. Bottom: the longest loop found, and how much of the net flow goes round. B1 10k: the thirty B1 worlds of 10,000 tokens (Experiment 2); B1 fixed: the same with brains that never change (Experiment 7); B1 100k: B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10); B1 sizes: B1 at 800 to 409,600 tokens (Experiment 8) and at 5,000 with and without a hidden layer (Experiments 12 and 13); B2 10k: the ten B2 worlds of Experiment 16; B2 var: B2 with one rule or rate changed (Experiments 9, 15 and 16); B2 5k: B2 at 5,000 tokens, with all its rules or with one taken away (Experiment 14) — except lapse: the condition in which any unused link lapses; B1 pil. and B2 pil.: the pilot worlds that play the engine's game.
every_world.recipe:
**Runs.** every simulation made so far, as `book/results/worlds.json` holds it (`python3 research/atlas/across.py lab`, `pilots`, `write`): a lab run's statistics are the means of its record over a stretch of iterations; a pilot's, of 20 games recorded from its checkpoint and summarised the same way.

**Data.** From each world's `cyclingShare`, `netFlowShare`, `lightningLongest` and `netCyclingShare` (gol_lightning.py, on the heavy rows of a run's record).

1. Take each world's mean over iterations 900–999, or 400–499 if it has no later one.
2. Put it in the first group of the list in book_chapters/everyworld.py it belongs to.
3. Draw one dot per world; the bar is each group's median.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py lightning`.

size.title: The longest loop grows with the world
size.caption: The longest loop the greedy search finds in a B1 world, against the world's size, both axes logarithmic: the median grows as the tokens to the power 0.31, so a world twice the size has loops 1.24 times as long. The blue line is the same after a token one way and a token back have cancelled.
size.recipe:
**Runs.** The B1 worlds of Experiment 8 (800 to 409,600 tokens, three seeds each, over iterations 400–499), of Experiments 12 and 2 (5,000 and 10,000 tokens) and of Experiment 10 (100,000 tokens), over iterations 900–999.

**Data.** From each world's mean `lightningLongest` and `netLightningLongest` in book/results/worlds.json.

1. Take each world's mean of the longest loop over its stretch.
2. Take the median at each size; fit a straight line to the logarithms.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py lightning`.

life.title: Through a world's life
life.caption: The two statistics through the life of thirty B1 worlds (Experiment 2) and ten B2 worlds (Experiment 16): the median at each recorded iteration, with the middle half of the worlds as a band.
life.recipe:
**Runs.** The thirty B1 worlds of Experiment 2 and the ten B2 worlds of Experiment 16, 10,000 tokens each.

**Data.** From `stats.jsonl`, the heavy rows (every 25th iteration).

1. Read each world's statistic at every heavy row.
2. Draw the median of the worlds and their middle half at each iteration.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py lightning`.

exact.title: A greedy count and an exact one
exact.caption: Each dot is a world: across, the exact share of the flow over 50 games that circulates (the Helmholtz–Hodge decomposition of [Gliders, and who helps whom](gliders-and-who-helps-whom.md)); up, the greedy loop count of a single game, averaged over the same thousand iterations.
exact.recipe:
**Runs.** The ten B2 worlds of Experiment 16 and the first ten B1 worlds of Experiment 2, iterations 1,000 to 2,000.

**Data.** From `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/circulation_20.json` (research/oee/checks/circulation.py) and each world's `cyclingShare`.

1. Take each world's circulating share, the median over its twenty windows of 50 games.
2. Take its mean greedy loop share over the same iterations.
3. Draw one against the other.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py lightning`.
